title: Canine Campus
description: Stockton Street Dogs / Street Dog Sanctuary proposes a campus for dogs without safe placement, including overflow and recovery care.
intended_outcome: Increase safe dog-care and placement capacity, including space for dogs recovering from veterinary treatment.

capacity_summary.headline: Proposed capacity: Hundreds of dogs
capacity_summary.how_it_helps: Could provide overflow sheltering and recovery care for dogs waiting for safe placement.
capacity_summary.not_yet_verified: Fundraising is documented; full funding, site, approvals, opening date, and usable operating capacity remain unverified.

demand_contribution: Could give dogs awaiting placement, shelter overflow, or medical recovery a safe care setting; none of that capacity is confirmed available.

expected_capacity_or_benefit.description: The proposal describes capacity for hundreds of dogs at a time; no funded or operating capacity is verified.

milestones.description: Stockton Streetdogs opened a construction fundraising campaign for the proposed Canine Campus; this does not establish full funding or an operating facility.

open_questions: Has a suitable site been secured?
How much funding is committed, and how much is still required?
Are permits or other approvals needed, and have they been obtained?
Is there a realistic construction and opening timeline?
What would the initial usable capacity be?
What staffing and operating support will be required?
Which volunteer roles would be approved and actionable?
next_verification_step: Request current project milestones, funding commitments and remaining needs, and site status directly from Stockton Street Dogs.

title: Stockton Animal Shelter expansion
description: City renovation and expansion of the Stockton Animal Shelter, including planned care and public-access improvements.
intended_outcome: Improve animal care, veterinary facilities, and adoption access; the net change in dog placement capacity is not yet established.

capacity_summary.headline: Construction underway: Expanded treatment and recovery facilities
capacity_summary.how_it_helps: New treatment, isolation, and rehabilitation space could improve care and help dogs move toward adoption.
capacity_summary.not_yet_verified: Completion, additional usable dog-care capacity, and effects on outcomes remain unverified.

demand_contribution: New treatment, isolation, rehabilitation, and public-access space could improve care and movement to adoption; net dog-place capacity and changed outcomes are unmeasured.

expected_capacity_or_benefit.description: Planned medical, isolation, rehabilitation, adoption-lobby, and other facility improvements; additional dog-care places have not been quantified.

milestones.description: City scheduled a groundbreaking after awarding the construction contract; the later field visit confirms work proceeded.
Crossover field visit observed the expansion under construction; this does not verify completion.

open_questions: What construction work remains and when will it be accepted?
When will each new space open for use?
How many additional dogs, if any, can be cared for at once?
What staffing and operating resources are required?
next_verification_step: Request the latest construction schedule and operational capacity plan from Stockton Animal Services.

title: Pet Wellness & Adoption Center
description: City of Stockton satellite animal resource center with Hard Luck Animal Welfare Advocates as a veterinary-services partner.
intended_outcome: Expand access to veterinary, wellness, and off-site adoption services.

capacity_summary.headline: Facility development reported complete
capacity_summary.how_it_helps: Wellness care could help owners keep dogs, while off-site adoption space could help dogs leave shelter care.
capacity_summary.not_yet_verified: Current services and measurable additional veterinary or adoption capacity remain unverified.

demand_contribution: Accessible veterinary care could prevent avoidable surrender, while off-site adoptions could help dogs leave care; actual incremental service volume is unverified.

expected_capacity_or_benefit.description: City plans describe expanded veterinary services and a calmer off-site adoption space; current service volume is unverified.

milestones.description: City reported a grand-opening ceremony; this does not establish which services are currently available.

open_questions: Which wellness, surgery, and adoption services are currently available?
What are the hours, eligibility, appointment rules, and actual service volumes?
What additional capacity is attributable to this center rather than existing contracts?
next_verification_step: Confirm current services, schedules, staffing, and completed procedures with Stockton Animal Services and Hard Luck.

title: Animal Balance spay/neuter contract
description: Separate three-month City contract with Animal Balance for high-volume shelter spay/neuter services.
intended_outcome: Reduce the shelter sterilization backlog and shorten delays before safe placement.

capacity_summary.headline: City-approved contract target: Approximately 200 pets
capacity_summary.how_it_helps: Completed sterilizations could reduce treatment backlogs and placement delays.
capacity_summary.not_yet_verified: Completed procedures, dog/cat split, and resulting care capacity remain unverified.

demand_contribution: If delivered, additional sterilizations could reduce backlog and future unplanned litters; completed procedures and effects on intake are unknown.

expected_capacity_or_benefit.description: Contract targeted approximately 200 pets across three clinic events; completed procedures and sustained capacity are unknown.

procedure_tracking.period: Approximate target across three events under the three-month contract approved 2026-01-13

milestones.description: City approved a three-month Animal Balance agreement; delivery remains unverified.

open_questions: How many procedures were completed, by date and species?
Did the agreement clear any backlog?
Was capacity retained after the three-month term?
next_verification_step: Obtain the Animal Balance contract performance report and reconcile planned versus completed procedures.

title: Hard Luck veterinary staffing expansion
description: City extension of its Hard Luck Animal Welfare Advocates agreement, with four additional positions; separate from the Animal Balance procedure contract.
intended_outcome: Increase veterinary and animal-care staffing available to Stockton Animal Services and related services.

capacity_summary.headline: Authorized: 4 additional positions
capacity_summary.how_it_helps: Filled veterinary and animal-care positions could expand treatment and sterilization capacity.
capacity_summary.not_yet_verified: Hiring completion and resulting care capacity remain unverified.

demand_contribution: Filled veterinary positions could expand treatment and sterilization throughput, reducing delays before placement; filled posts and output are unknown.

expected_capacity_or_benefit.description: Four additional contract positions were authorized; filled positions, procedure counts, and net capacity remain unknown.

milestones.description: City approved a one-year extension and four additional positions; hiring and service delivery remain unverified.

open_questions: Were all four positions filled, and when?
Which services and locations gained capacity?
How many additional spay/neuter procedures or treatment appointments resulted?
next_verification_step: Confirm staffing and service outputs with the City and Hard Luck, keeping them separate from Animal Balance totals.

title: Pathways Neighborhood
description: Existing St. Mary's Community Services modular transitional-housing project, tracked here because housing access may affect whether people can remain with dogs.
intended_outcome: Provide transitional housing and supportive services that help residents move toward permanent housing; Pathways pet admission is unverified.

actual_additional_capacity.description: Reported 268 transitional-housing beds; dog-inclusive placements and eligible dog capacity are unknown.

capacity_summary.headline: Operational facility: 268 reported housing beds
capacity_summary.how_it_helps: Transitional housing could help people remain with dogs if Pathways admits pets.
capacity_summary.not_yet_verified: Dog-admission rules, dog-inclusive capacity, and actual dog-inclusive placements remain unverified.

demand_contribution: Could help people and dogs remain together only if Pathways itself admits dogs; that policy and actual dog-inclusive placements are unverified.

expected_capacity_or_benefit.description: Provide transitional housing and on-site support toward permanent housing; pet-inclusive benefit remains unverified.

milestones.description: St. Mary's held a Pathways open house and described the project as up and running.

open_questions: Does Pathways itself admit residents with dogs, and under what rules?
Are there breed, size, vaccination, or behavior restrictions?
How many residents with dogs have been served?
next_verification_step: Ask St. Mary's for Pathways-specific pet policy and actual pet-inclusive placements; do not infer them from campus-wide pet care.
